title: VPD Clear Langley RCMP Officer in Fatal 2010 Shooting
article: Vancouver Police said Wednesday that there were no grounds to consider criminal charges against a Langley RCMP officer who fatally shot Jeffrey James Alvin Wright last year.
Const. Lindsey Houghton wouldn't say too much else about the VPD investigation, pending a Coroner's inquest that will be held in March 2012.

But lawyer Donald Sorochan, who is representing Wright's young widow Heather, said he has a problem with the whole process. He said that in order to instill public confidence in the VPD's investigation, the matter should have been reviewed by the criminal justice branch of the Attorney General's ministry.

Heather has filed a lawsuit against the RCMP, the B.C. Solicitor General and others in connection with Wright's death. The suit says that when Heather called 911 about 11:26 p.m. on Aug. 6, 2010, she did not allege any violence. But she was looking for police assistance to enter her home because she had an argument with Wright, who had gone to bed.

Sorochan said Wright was shot in the bedroom. When RCMP went into that bedroom, a struggle ensued and Wright was fatally shot in the stomach. Sorochan still doesn't know what the 911 call said, what the officers involved said in their statements to VPD because none of the evidence has yet been released to him. He didn't push for disclosure yet because he wanted to respect the police investigation, he said.
Sorochan has been involved in cases and inquiries involving police oversight in B.C. since 1974 and he is a big advocate for change.
Just last week, Saanich police cleared a Surrey RCMP officer in the fatal shooting of Adam Purdie last March. Again the case was not sent to Crown prosecutors for review.

Sorochan says that even if police investigating have made the right call, it is important to have Crown do the final review, simply because of the public's perception or distrust of police investigating police.
